A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IGen and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite substantial figure redesign and supplementary-section renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-reconstruction measurements, generated-behavior evaluations, computational measurements, and real-robot policy results in Section 4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds training-budget results and a qualitative component ablation.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 now explicitly describes VLM identification of task-relevant objects before SAM segmentation; v1 specifies the resulting masks without this step. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes the procedure or documents previously implicit processing. The remaining pipeline and equations are retained.

E1.justification: Simpler, DreamGen Bench, and the open-world and real-robot manipulation coverage remain. Hit Box and toy placement receive greater quantitative prominence in v2, but both already appear in v1's appendix. No additional dataset or distinct task requirement is established.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparisons retain Real-to-Sim, Cosmos-Predict2, and TesserAct. Real-robot comparisons retain zero-shot policies and policies trained on 10 or 100 human demonstrations. The added 100-sample IGen condition changes its training budget rather than introducing another baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 7 adds a 100-sample IGen condition and evaluates success against data-generation time, including averages across three tasks. Section 4.1 and Table 1 remove FID. The appendix retains the deployment-trial protocol, training steps, batch size, and hardware.

E4.justification: New supplementary Figure 17 provides a qualitative example disabling reconstruction, keypoint guidance, and multistep planning. Figure 7 extends synthetic-data scaling from one training size to two. Conversely, v1 Figure 8's human-versus-IGen trajectory case study is removed. These are limited analytical additions and removals.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 12 independent deployment trials per task. Neither introduces training-seed information, repeated-training estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 7 adds Hit Box and 100-sample IGen results, reporting three-task averages of 44.5%/66.7% for IGen versus 19.4%/58.3% for human data at corresponding time budgets. These are not directly comparable with v1's two-task, per-task bars. FID entries and the old trajectory case are removed, and qualitative ablation outcomes are added. Other Table 1 scores and Figures 4–5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The keypoint and pose representations, rigid-motion equations, and point-cloud composition remain unchanged, including Equations 1–3. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same claims: scalable image-derived visuomotor data, generation without human demonstrations, and successful real-world policy transfer. Local wording edits and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 removes the explicit limitation concerning dependence on foundation vision models and visually defective inputs. Its new ablation attributes failures to incomplete reconstruction, missing keypoint-based spatial computation, and absent obstacle avoidance. Section 4.3 also interprets policy performance through matched data-collection time budgets.

D1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 add details about VLM object identification and inference of translation distances and lift heights. Supplementary Figure 18 supplies an annotated image, keypoint coordinates, and task instruction illustrating VLM inputs. Existing training, simulation, hardware, and project-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Grounding DINO as reference 43 alongside SAM in Section 3.1. The previously cited works and the broader positioning against simulation-based and video-generation approaches remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized prose revisions, expanded affiliations, new acknowledgements, and revised experimental discussion. Appendix sections A–D become Sections 6–9, followed by two new sections. The main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 6 are substantially redesigned, and Figure 7 changes from task-specific bars to time-versus-success curves with task and average traces. Table 1 loses its FID columns, v1 Figure 8 disappears, supplementary randomization figures are enlarged and relocated, and Figures 17–18 are added.

improvement.justification: The added training-budget comparison and component ablation make data efficiency and design choices more assessable, while the keypoint example improves technical clarity. These provide a modest net benefit. The gains are limited by qualitative-only ablation evidence and unchanged uncertainty reporting; removing the limitations paragraph and inconsistent Place Toy versus Place Bottle labeling weaken transparency.
